681	### Sensitive-field identification
682	
683	Sensitive-field identification produces candidate annotations for the fields of
684	a schema version. It complements the manual privacy policies but never creates
685	or modifies one: an identification is advisory only. Records (including their
686	stable ids) persist across restarts.
687	
688	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
689	  identify one field. The body contains exactly `field` and `samples`:
690	  `{"field": "contact_email", "samples": ["alice@example.com"]}`. `field` must
691	  name an existing field of the version; its name and type are taken from the
692	  version definition. `samples` is an array of JSON scalars (strings, numbers,
693	  booleans or `null`) and may be empty; objects or arrays reject the whole
694	  request. The samples are never stored or echoed back. Returns the record;
695	  the first submission for a field returns `201`, re-running the same field
696	  refreshes the record in place (the id is unchanged) and returns `200`.
697	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
698	  return every identification record of the version sorted by id ascending
699	  (empty when there are none). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
700	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
701	
702	  Each record has `id`, `field`, `field_type`, `evidence`, `confidence`,
703	  `source` and `created_at`. `source` references the identified field as
704	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`. `evidence` is the ordered, de-duplicated
705	  list of hit kinds, name hits before sample hits:
706	
707	  - **Name hits** — the field name contains a sensitive word case-insensitively
708	    as a substring. The words are `email`, `phone`, `id_card`, `password`,
709	    `token` and `birth`, emitting `name:<word>` in that order.
710	  - **Sample hits** — only string sample values are inspected (numbers,
711	    booleans and `null` never hit), and only when the field's declared type is
712	    `string`; a field declared with any other type is matched by name alone,
713	    even when a sample looks like an email. `sample:email` requires exactly
714	    one `@` with non-empty text on both sides and a dot in the domain;
715	    `sample:phone` requires an 11-digit string starting with `1`. Either format
716	    matching is sufficient.
717	
718	  `confidence` is `high` when both the name and the samples hit, `medium` for
719	  samples only, `low` for the name only and `none` when neither side hits
720	  (`evidence` is then an empty list but the record is still generated).
721	
722	  One record is kept per field: a re-run overwrites the evidence and confidence
723	  in place with a stable id. Unknown dataset/version → `404`; a field that does
724	  not exist in the version → `404`; missing or extra body fields, a
725	  non-string or blank field name, a `samples` value that is not an array of
726	  scalars (objects and arrays included), an empty body, malformed JSON or any
727	  query parameter → `422` and nothing is written.
728	
729	#### Masking strategy suggestions
730	
731	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions`
732	  — read-only advisory masking-strategy candidates derived from the version's
733	  identification records. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
734	  parameters (`422` if either is present, with nothing written); unknown
735	  dataset/version → `404`. A version without identification records returns an
736	  empty list rather than an error.
737	
738	  Each candidate has exactly `field`, `classification`, `masking` and
739	  `allowed_roles`. Only records whose name or samples hit produce a candidate;
740	  a record with empty evidence is omitted. Candidates follow the identification
741	  records' `id` ascending and are recomputed on every read, so refreshing an
742	  identification changes the suggestion on the next request. The endpoint
743	  writes nothing, never registers a privacy policy and leaves the
744	  identification records' fields, ordering and refresh semantics untouched;
745	  the privacy view continues to mask according to registered policies only.
746	
747	  - `classification` is `PII` for email, phone, id-card and birthday hits, and
748	    `CREDENTIAL` for password and token hits. A field hitting both is `PII`.
749	  - `masking` reuses the privacy-view vocabulary: `partial` for `PII`
750	    candidates and `redact` for `CREDENTIAL` candidates (a both-kinds field
751	    takes `partial`); no new masking format is introduced.
752	  - `allowed_roles` is always an empty list: the suggested masking applies to
753	    every role, granting none an unmasked view.
754	
755	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions/register`
756	  — turn the current advisory candidates into registered privacy policies. The
757	  body contains only `{"fields": ["<field>", ...]}`: a non-empty array of
758	  distinct field names, each non-empty after trimming and naming an existing
759	  field of the version that currently has a masking suggestion candidate.
760	  Returns `201` with one privacy policy record per requested field, in the
761	  request's field-name order; each record has the same fields as the manual
762	  policy creation response (`id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`,
763	  `allowed_roles`, `enabled`, `created_at`), is enabled by default and gets a
764	  service-generated id and timestamp. Each policy copies its candidate's
765	  `classification` and `masking` verbatim with the candidate's empty
766	  `allowed_roles`, so after registration every role sees those fields masked;
767	  the next privacy view read masks according to the new policies. The whole
768	  batch is validated before anything is written, so any rejection writes no
769	  policy and no timestamp. Unknown dataset/version, or a named field that does
770	  not exist in the version → `404`; a field without an available candidate
771	  (never identified, or whose identification record currently yields no
772	  candidate) or one that already has a privacy policy → `409`; two concurrent
773	  registrations of the same field leave exactly one winner. Missing or extra
774	  body fields, an empty `fields` array, duplicate, non-string or blank names,
775	  an empty body, a whitespace-only body, malformed JSON or any query parameter
776	  → `422` and nothing is written. Registration only reads the identification
777	  records and field definitions; it never writes or auto-refreshes an
778	  identification, and the read-only suggestions endpoint stays unchanged.
779	
780	### Row snapshots
781	
782	A row snapshot persistently records the rows of a schema version at one point in
783	time. Snapshots (including their rows) survive restarts.
784	
785	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — persist a snapshot.
786	  Body: `{"rows": [{...}, ...]}` where `rows` must be an array of JSON objects
787	  (it may be empty). The JSON values and the order of rows/object keys are deep
788	  copied verbatim. Returns `201` with `id`, `dataset`, `version`,
789	  `created_at` and `row_count` (no rows). Unknown dataset/version → `404`;
790	  malformed or non-object rows → `422` and nothing is written.
791	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — list snapshot
792	  metadata sorted by `id` ascending (no `rows`).
793	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}` — return
794	  the metadata together with the saved `rows`. Unknown dataset/version/snapshot
795	  → `404`.
796	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at?timestamp=<ISO-8601>` —
797	  return the most recent snapshot whose `created_at` is not later than
798	  `timestamp`, including its rows. The timestamp must be a timezone-aware
799	  ISO-8601 date-time (an offset or trailing `Z`): missing, invalid or
800	  timezone-less values return `422`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; when no
801	  snapshot exists at or before the timestamp the response is `404`.
802	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at/diff?from=<ISO-8601>&to=<ISO-8601>`
803	  — read-only time-travel row diff, appended one segment after the bare-row
804	  time lookup and accepting GET only. Each of `from` (the baseline) and `to`
805	  (the target) must be a timezone-aware ISO-8601 date-time; each side
806	  independently selects the latest snapshot whose `created_at` is not later
807	  than its own timestamp (the same selection as the bare-row lookup), so the
808	  two times may resolve to the same snapshot and a `to` earlier than `from` is
809	  valid — the two snapshots are simply compared in their named order. The
810	  comparison reads snapshots and rows and writes nothing. The JSON document
811	  is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
812	  newline) with top-level keys `from_timestamp`, `to_timestamp`,
813	  `from_snapshot_id`, `to_snapshot_id`, `added`, `removed`, `fields_added`
814	  and `fields_removed` in that order; the timestamps echo the submitted query
815	  values. `added` and `removed` use the exact comparison semantics of the
816	  snapshot-id diff (JSON-object multisets, key order irrelevant, array order
817	  and value types significant, duplicates counted; entries
818	  `{"row", "count"}` sorted by canonical row text). `fields_added` and
819	  `fields_removed` compare the top-level field names appearing on the
820	  snapshots' row objects: names only on the target side are added, names only
821	  on the baseline side are removed, names on both enter neither set, and each
822	  list sorts by field name ascending. When both times select the same
823	  snapshot all four collections are empty and the request succeeds. Unknown
824	  dataset/version → `404`, checked before every request-shape check; a missing,
825	  blank, repeated, unparseable or timezone-less `from`/`to`, an extra query
826	  parameter or any request body bytes (whitespace-only included) → `422`; a
827	  side with no snapshot at or before its timestamp → `404` and nothing is
828	  written.
829	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at/masked-view` —
830	  role-masked time travel, appended one segment after the bare-row time
831	  lookup and accepting POST only. The body contains exactly `role` and
832	  `timestamp`: `{"role": "guest", "timestamp": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`; the
833	  service selects the latest snapshot whose `created_at` is not later than
834	  `timestamp` (the same selection as the bare-row lookup). On success it
835	  returns `{"dataset", "version", "snapshot_id", "created_at", "rows"}`; the
836	  `rows` are an order-preserving copy of the snapshot's rows masked exactly
837	  as the row-submission privacy view masks them, applying only the version's
838	  currently enabled policies (`redact`/`partial` semantics, `allowed_roles`,
839	  nulls and uncovered fields behave identically). Every successful read
840	  appends one masking-hit record per value actually masked, structurally
841	  identical to the regular view's hit records and continuing the same
842	  per-version sequence run, plus exactly one access record whose
843	  `row_count` is the snapshot's row count and whose `masked_count` equals
844	  the number of hit records written by the read. An empty snapshot, an
845	  allowed role, all-null values and a version without policies all succeed
846	  and leave only the access record. The records enter all existing
847	  masking-hit/access reads, filters, summaries, diffs, reconciliation,
848	  trends and cleanup previews; records of one read share a write timestamp,
849	  sequences stay continuous across processes, and a write obstruction never
850	  fails the read. The read never modifies or deletes the snapshot or its
851	  rows and never changes policies or identification records. Unknown
852	  dataset/version → `404`, and no snapshot existing at or before the
853	  timestamp is likewise `404`, both checked before every shape check (the
854	  latter whenever the body carries a usable timestamp); a missing or
855	  wrong-typed `role`/`timestamp`, a role blank after trimming, an
856	  unparseable or timezone-less timestamp, an extra body field, an empty,
857	  whitespace-only or non-JSON body, a non-object body and any query
858	  parameter are `422` and write nothing.
859	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/diff/{other_snapshot_id}` —
860	  compare two snapshots as JSON-object multisets. Object key order does not
861	  affect equality, while array order and JSON value types do (e.g. `1`, `1.0`,
862	  `"1"` and `true` are all distinct), and duplicate rows are counted. Both
863	  snapshots must belong to the dataset and version named in the path, otherwise
864	  `422`; unknown dataset/version/snapshot → `404`. The response is
865	  `{"from_snapshot_id", "to_snapshot_id", "added", "removed"}`; `added` lists
866	  rows present more often (or only) in the `to` snapshot and `removed` the
867	  converse, each entry being `{"row": {...}, "count": <int>}` sorted by the
868	  canonical (key-sorted) JSON text of `row`.
869	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/quality-rules/evaluate`
870	  — evaluate the version's enabled quality rules over the snapshot's persisted
871	  rows. The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`);
872	  unknown dataset/version/snapshot → `404` (checked first), and a snapshot
873	  owned by another version → `422`. The response and the rule semantics are
874	  exactly those of the row-submission evaluation (`{"dataset", "version",
875	  "results"}`), the snapshot and its rows are never modified, and every
876	  successful evaluation appends the same immutable history summary (with
877	  `row_count` set to the snapshot's actual row count) that also feeds the
878	  evaluation diff and anomaly detection. An empty snapshot is recorded with
879	  zero violations.
880	
881	### Retention policies and lineage-aware snapshot deletion
882	
883	A schema version can carry a single retention policy; snapshot deletion is a
884	two-stage request/confirm flow that refuses to remove snapshots still feeding
885	downstream fields. Policies and requests are persisted across restarts.
886	
887	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/retention-policies` — create the
888	  version's one retention policy. Body: `{"retention_days": 30}` with a
889	  non-negative integer. Returns `201` with `id`, `dataset`, `version`,
890	  `retention_days`, `created_at`. A second policy for the same version returns
891	  `409`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; other invalid input → `422`.
892	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/deletion-requests` —
893	  request deletion. Body contains only a non-empty `reason`. The snapshot and
894	  the version's retention policy must exist. Returns `201` with `id`,
895	  `snapshot_id`, `policy_id`, `reason`, `status`, `impacted`, `created_at`.
896	  `impacted` lists every field directly or indirectly reachable downstream of
897	  any field of the snapshot's version along lineage mappings; entries are
898	  deduplicated and sorted by dataset, version and field ascending. The request
899	  is `blocked` when any downstream field exists and `pending` otherwise. A
900	  second `pending`/`blocked` request for the same snapshot returns `409`.
901	- `GET .../snapshots/{snapshot_id}/deletion-requests` — list the snapshot's
902	  deletion requests sorted by `id` ascending. The collection remains
903	  addressable after a confirmed request has deleted its snapshot.
904	- `POST .../snapshots/{snapshot_id}/deletion-requests/{request_id}/confirm` —
905	  confirm a request (no body). Confirmation succeeds only while the request is
906	  `pending` and the snapshot is at least `retention_days` old; otherwise `409`
907	  and nothing is deleted. On success the snapshot is deleted atomically with
908	  the status change to `confirmed`, and the response adds `confirmed_at`. Once
909	  deleted, the snapshot no longer appears in snapshot read, list, `at` or diff
910	  responses.
911	
912	  Unknown dataset/version/snapshot/policy/request → `404`; other invalid input
913	  → `422` and nothing is written.
914	
915	### Processing tasks
916	
917	A processing task is a named unit of work attached to a schema version; each
918	run records one attempt. Tasks and runs are persisted across restarts.
919	
920	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks` — create a
921	  task. Body: `{"name": "extract", "depends_on": [1], "max_attempts": 3}`.
922	  `name` must be non-empty and unique within the version (`409` on conflict);
923	  `depends_on` is an array of distinct task ids from the same version (default
924	  `[]`, unknown ids → `404`); `max_attempts` is a positive integer (default
925	  `1`). Returns `201` with `id`, `dataset`, `version`, `name`, `depends_on`,
926	  `max_attempts`, `status` (`pending`), `attempt_count` (`0`) and
927	  `created_at`. Other invalid input → `422` and nothing is written.
928	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks` — list tasks
929	  sorted by `id` ascending.
930	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}` —
931	  return the task together with its `runs`, sorted by `attempt` ascending.
932	  Each run has `id`, `task_id`, `attempt`, `status`, `started_at`,
933	  `finished_at` and `error`. Unknown dataset/version/task → `404`.
934	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs` —
935	  start a new run. Only allowed while the task is `pending` or `failed`, has
936	  attempts left (`attempt_count < max_attempts`) and every task in
937	  `depends_on` has status `succeeded`; otherwise `409` and nothing is written.
938	  Returns `201` with the new `running` run and increments the task's
939	  `attempt_count` (the task becomes `running`).
940	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/dispatch` —
941	  worker batch claim. The body is optional and contains only an optional
942	  `limit`: omit the body (or send `{}`) to claim one task, or send
943	  `{"limit": <positive integer>}`. Within a single transaction, up to `limit`
944	  startable tasks are selected by task id ascending; a task is startable when
945	  it is `pending`, or `failed` with attempts left, and every direct dependency
946	  is `succeeded` at selection time. Each selected task gets a new `running`
947	  run for its next attempt, `attempt_count` is incremented and the task becomes
948	  `running`. `running`, `succeeded`, attempt-exhausted and dependency-blocked
949	  tasks are skipped; a task started earlier in the same request is only
950	  `running`, so its dependents are not selectable until a later request.
951	  Returns `201` with `{"dataset", "version", "runs"}`; `runs` is sorted by
952	  task id ascending and each run has the same fields as the single-task start
953	  endpoint. When no task is startable the response is still `201` with an
954	  empty `runs` list. Concurrent dispatches (and dispatches interleaved with
955	  single-task starts) never create a duplicate attempt or two running runs for
956	  the same task, and a single response never exceeds `limit`. Unknown
957	  dataset/version → `404`; extra body fields, a non-integer (including
958	  boolean) or non-positive `limit` → `422` and nothing is written.
959	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}` —
960	  finish the currently running run. Body: `{"status": "succeeded"}` or
961	  `{"status": "failed", "error": "<non-empty message>"}`. Writes `finished_at`
962	  and moves the task to the same status; a `failed` task with attempts left
963	  can be started again. Finishing an already finished run → `409`; a run that
964	  does not belong to the task/version in the path → `422`; unknown
965	  dataset/version/task/run → `404`; other invalid input → `422` and nothing
966	  is written.
967	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/batch-complete` —
968	  finish several currently running runs in one transaction. Body contains only
969	  a non-empty `runs` array; each item names a task of the path version and one
970	  of its runs: `{"task_id": <int>, "run_id": <int>, "status": "succeeded"}` or
971	  the same with `"status": "failed"` and an `error` that is non-empty after
972	  trimming whitespace (`succeeded` items carry no `error`). The same task must
973	  not appear twice. The whole batch is validated before any write and either
974	  every item completes or none do; on success the response is
975	  `{"dataset", "version", "runs"}` with the completed runs sorted by task id
976	  ascending, each carrying the same fields as the single-run finish response.
977	  Every run gets a `finished_at` timestamp and its task moves atomically to
978	  the same status; `failed` tasks keep their consumed attempts and stay
979	  retryable while attempts remain. Tasks whose dependencies succeed in the
980	  same batch are not started or skipped within that batch (the dependencies
981	  are `running` at selection time, as with dispatch) and become startable
982	  immediately afterwards, each at its next continuous attempt. Empty/missing
983	  `runs`, extra fields, non-integer (including boolean) ids, an unknown status
984	  or a missing/blank/non-string `error` → `422`; an empty body or malformed
985	  JSON → `422`; any query parameter → `422`. Unknown dataset/version → `404`;
986	  a batch task that does not exist or belongs to another dataset/version →
987	  `404`; an unknown run → `404` (a run belonging to another dataset/version is
988	  treated as out of scope); a run that belongs to another task of the same
989	  version → `422`. An already finished run, a duplicate task in the batch or a
990	  task that is not currently `running` (not currently completable) → `409`,
991	  and the entire batch is rolled back: statuses, timestamps and counters are
992	  unchanged. Concurrent batch completion is single-winner against the
993	  single-run finish/cancel endpoints, run starts and batch dispatch: exactly
994	  one racing operation commits and the others receive `409`, never leaving a
995	  `running` run with a half-written `finished_at` or rolling `attempt_count`
996	  back. Audit records appended afterwards record the run's terminal status,
997	  and the schedule, audit report and post-restart reads present the batch
998	  results through the existing fields and ordering.
999	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}/cancel` —
1000	  cancel the currently running run. The body contains only a non-empty
1001	  `reason` string; leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed and the result
1002	  is stored as the run's `error`. Returns the updated run with `finished_at`
1003	  written and `status` `failed`; the task is atomically moved to `failed` in
1004	  the same transaction while `attempt_count` is not rolled back, so a
1005	  cancelled task follows the existing start rules: it can run again when its
1006	  dependencies have succeeded and attempts remain, and the next run keeps the
1007	  continuous attempt sequence. Only a `running` run can be cancelled;
1008	  cancelling an already `succeeded`/`failed` run returns `409` and changes no
1009	  field. A run that does not belong to the task/version in the path → `422`;
1010	  unknown dataset/version/task/run → `404`; a missing reason, an extra body
1011	  field, a non-string reason or one that is blank after trimming, an empty
1012	  body, malformed JSON or any query parameter → `422` and nothing is
1013	  written. Cancellation is single-winner against finishing, single-task
1014	  starts and batch dispatch: exactly one racing operation performs the state
1015	  transition and the others receive `409`, so no run is left `running` with a
1016	  half-written `finished_at`.
1017	- `PUT /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/dependencies` —
1018	  atomically replace the task's dependency list. Body contains only
1019	  `{"depends_on": [<task id>, ...]}` (the array may be empty); the ids must
1020	  reference existing tasks of the same version without duplicates and must not
1021	  include the target task itself. The replacement is rejected when the target
1022	  task is not `pending` or when it would introduce a cycle in the dependency
1023	  graph; on success the updated task is returned. Unknown
1024	  dataset/version/task/dependency → `404`; a self dependency, a cycle or a
1025	  non-`pending` target → `409`; any other invalid body → `422` and nothing is
1026	  written. The existing run-start rule uses the updated dependencies.
1027	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/schedule` —
1028	  return `{"dataset", "version", "tasks"}` with tasks sorted by `id` ascending.
1029	  Each task carries every processing-task field plus `schedule_state` and
1030	  `blocking_task_ids`. `schedule_state` is `running` or `succeeded` for tasks
1031	  in those states; a `failed` task is `retryable` while attempts remain and
1032	  `exhausted` once they are used up; a `pending` task is `ready` when all of
1033	  its direct dependencies have succeeded, `upstream_failed` when any
1034	  dependency chain contains an `exhausted` or `upstream_failed` task, and
1035	  `blocked` otherwise. `blocking_task_ids` lists the direct dependencies that
1036	  have not succeeded, sorted ascending; it is empty for non-pending tasks.
1037	  States are recomputed on every read (including after a successful retry)
1038	  and both the dependency graph and the schedule survive restarts.
1039	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/audit-report` —
1040	  read-only audit report for the whole version; the endpoint takes no request
1041	  body and no query parameters (both are rejected with `422`; unknown
1042	  dataset/version → `404`). Returns
1043	  `{"dataset", "version", "summary", "tasks"}`. `summary` contains
1044	  `task_count`, `run_count`, `pending_tasks`, `running_tasks`,
1045	  `succeeded_tasks`, `failed_tasks`, `exhausted_tasks` and
1046	  `invalid_audit_runs`; status counters count tasks by their stored status,
1047	  `exhausted_tasks` counts `failed` tasks that have used up
1048	  `max_attempts`, and `invalid_audit_runs` counts runs whose audit chain fails
1049	  re-verification. `tasks` is sorted by task `id` and each task carries every
1050	  processing-task field plus `runs`; `runs` is sorted by `attempt` and each
1051	  run carries its run fields plus `proof`. `proof` re-runs the same checks as
1052	  the per-run verify endpoint over that run's audit chain and is
1053	  `{"valid", "checked_count", "last_evidence_hash"}`; `last_evidence_hash` is
1054	  the stored evidence hash of the chain's final record and is `null` only for
1055	  an empty chain — it is still returned when `valid` is `false`, and the run
1056	  details are retained. Summary counters always agree with the returned
1057	  details and the report is deterministic across restarts.
1058	
1059	### Processing run audit records (append-only proof chain)
1060	
1061	Every run carries an independent, tamper-evident chain of audit records.
1062	Records are append-only (the database rejects updates and deletes, and there
1063	are no per-record HTTP routes), numbered from `1` per run and linked through
1064	SHA-256 evidence hashes. They persist across restarts.
1065	
1066	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}/audit-records` —
1067	  append a record. Body contains exactly `event`, `input_summary` and
1068	  `result_summary`, each a string that is non-empty after trimming whitespace.
1069	  Returns `201` with the submitted fields plus `id`, `sequence` (continuous
1070	  from `1` within the run), `run_status` (the run's status at write time:
1071	  `running`/`succeeded`/`failed`), `previous_hash` (`null` for the first
1072	  record, otherwise the previous record's `evidence_hash`), `evidence_hash`
1073	  and `created_at`. Missing, extra, non-string or blank fields → `422` and
1074	  nothing is written; unknown dataset/version/task/run → `404`; a run that
1075	  does not belong to the path task (including one in another version) →
1076	  `422`. Concurrent appends never reuse a sequence or break the chain.
1077	- `GET .../runs/{run_id}/audit-records` — list the run's records in ascending
1078	  `sequence` order. Same `404`/`422` path rules.
1079	- `GET .../runs/{run_id}/audit-records/verify` — verify the chain. Returns the
1080	  path identifiers together with `valid` and `checked_count`:
1081	  `{"dataset", "version", "task_id", "run_id", "valid", "checked_count"}`.
1082	  Verification recomputes every `evidence_hash`, checks that `sequence` values
1083	  are continuous from `1` and that each `previous_hash` equals the preceding
1084	  record's `evidence_hash` (the first must be `null`). An intact chain returns
1085	  `"valid": true` (also for an empty chain).
1086	
1087	`evidence_hash` is the hexadecimal SHA-256 of a canonical JSON document built
1088	from every stored field except `id`, `created_at` and `evidence_hash` itself
1089	(`event`, `input_summary`, `result_summary`, `sequence`, `run_status`,
1090	`previous_hash`): keys are sorted by Unicode code point, no insignificant
1091	whitespace is emitted and the text is UTF-8 encoded.
1092
